title: Answer After a Deterministic Instruction
statement: Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register machine whose instruction at state $l$ is the deterministic instruction $i$. For any Boolean value $\beta$, register valuation $v$, recorded answer $r$, natural number $N$, and Boolean value $b$, a length-$(N+1)$ choice sequence that leaves answer $b$ from $(l,v,r)$ exists if and only if a length-$N$ choice sequence that leaves answer $b$ exists from the configuration obtained by one deterministic step using the machine that follows $A$'s deterministic instructions and replaces each choice instruction by an immediate return of $\beta$.
hypotheses_covered: A(l) is the deterministic instruction i
